title: ATANH has three regimes—subnormal DAZ to +0, binary64 x + x^3/3, and signed x87 ratio-log—breaking oddness above 0x3f1af82b729c1d83
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20228 and 20430, ATANH(x) returns #NUM! for |x| >= 1, flushes both signs of any subnormal input to +0 (0x0000000000000000), evaluates ordinary binary64 x + (x*x*x)/3 for normal |x| below 0x3f1af82b729c1d83 (~1.02880227e-4), and switches at 0x3f1af82b729c1d83 to 0.5 * LN(RN53(RN64(RN53(RN64(1+x)) / RN53(RN64(1-x))))). Because the ratio branch evaluates 1+x and 1-x directly without taking |x|, ATANH(-x) != -ATANH(x) in that regime: at ±0x3f1af82b729c1d83 the positive and negative outputs differ by 4,314 ULPs (0x3f1af82b7434c926 vs 0xbf1af82b7434b84c). All 22,008 full-bank ATANH rows match.
basis: Measured across Excel 16.0 build 20228 W109 switch/held-out campaigns (CalcFunc-Evidence work/w109/G4-02-atanh/) and build 20430, matching 22,008/22,008 full-bank ATANH rows.
inferred: At +0x3f1af82b729c1d82, the cubic and ratio-log bodies produce the same binary64 bits, so the exact switch selection between +0x3f1af82b729c1d82 and +0x3f1af82b729c1d83 rests on the negative-input asymmetry at 0xbf1af82b729c1d83.
